comment: Every fixed utterance the voice guide speaks. ml/generate_audio.py synthesizes one clip per entry into public/audio/ and writes manifest.json keyed by normalized text. The app falls back to speechSynthesis for any missing clip.
prompts: Welcome. Before we begin, let us check the sound. If you can hear my voice, tap the large button on the screen now.
Good. Now pick up the pen and draw a line inside the white box. Then tap Next.
You are ready to begin. There are thirteen short tasks. I will explain each one. Work at your own pace. Tap Start when you are ready.
I did not see a line yet. Please draw a line inside the white box first.

Please draw a line going from a number to a letter, in increasing order, using the pen. Begin at the circle marked one, and trace over the dotted line to A, and then to two. Then continue on your own: draw from two to B, and keep switching between numbers and letters until you reach the circle marked E.
Copy this drawing as accurately as you can in the space on the right. Tap Done when you are finished.
Now, draw a clock. Put in all the numbers, and set the time to ten past eleven. Tap Done when you are finished.
Tell me the name of this animal.
Please say the name of the animal now.
This is a memory test. I am going to read you a list of five words that you will have to remember now, and later on. Listen carefully.
I am going to read the same list one more time. Try to remember and tell me as many words as you can, including words you said the first time.
Now, tell me as many of those words as you can remember.
I will ask you to recall those words again at the end of the test.
I am going to say some numbers. When I am done, repeat them to me exactly as I said them.
Now I am going to say some more numbers. But this time, when I am done, repeat them to me in the backward order.
Please say the numbers now.
Please enter the numbers using the keypad, then tap OK.
I am going to read a list of letters. Every time I say the letter A, tap the large button once. If I say a different letter, do not tap.

Now, I will ask you to count by subtracting seven from one hundred, and then, keep subtracting seven from your answer until I tell you to stop. Say each number out loud. Begin now: what is one hundred minus seven?
Stop. Well done.
I am going to read you a sentence. Repeat it after me, exactly as I say it.
Now I am going to read you another sentence. Repeat it after me, exactly as I say it.
I only know that John is the one to help today
The cat always hid under the couch when dogs were in the room
Please repeat the sentence now.
Tell me as many words as you can think of that begin with the letter F. Proper nouns like names of people or places do not count, and numbers do not count. You will have one minute. Ready? Begin.
Time is up. Well done.
Tell me how an orange and a banana are alike. What do they have in common?
Yes, and they are also both fruit.
Now, tell me how a train and a bicycle are alike.
Now, tell me how a watch and a ruler are alike.
Please say your answer now.
Earlier in the test, I read you a list of five words and asked you to remember them. Tell me as many of those words as you can remember now.
Take your time. Say any of the words you remember now.
I will give you a hint. One of the words was a part of the body. What was the word?
I will give you a hint. One of the words was a type of fabric. What was the word?
I will give you a hint. One of the words was a type of building. What was the word?
I will give you a hint. One of the words was a type of flower. What was the word?
I will give you a hint. One of the words was a color. What was the word?
Was it nose, face, or hand?
Was it denim, cotton, or velvet?
Was it church, school, or hospital?
Was it rose, daisy, or tulip?
Was it red, blue, or green?
Tell me the date today. What day of the month is it?
What month is it?
What year is it?
What day of the week is it?
Tell me the name of this place. Where are you right now?
Which city are you in?

tokens.comment: Single-item clips for paced sequences (1 per second): vigilance letters, digit-span digits, memory words. Spoken text may differ from the on-app token (letters get 'ay/bee/see' style phrasing automatic in TTS).
